name: People, Work and Organisations
focus: Behaviour in organisations: individual differences, motivation and engagement, teams, power, politics and conflict, organisation design, organisational culture and organisational change.
units: Unit 1 Understanding behaviour in organisations: key schools of thought in OB; contemporary perspectives on organisations; contemporary influences on the world of work; managing in the 21st century
Unit 2 Individual differences: how people differ; personality; intelligence and mindsets; attitudes, beliefs and values; perception; neurodiversity; managing individual differences
Unit 3 Motivation and engagement: how to motivate people at work; theories of motivation; job design; performance management; engagement
Unit 4 Team dynamics: understanding groups and teams; building and developing effective teams; downsides of teams; teams in the 21st century
Unit 5 Power, politics and conflict: organisational power; organisational politics; organisational conflict
Unit 6 Designing effective organisations: what organisation design is; features of organisation structures; types of structures; approaches to structural design; formal and informal organisations
Unit 7 Organisational culture: what culture is; typologies of culture; the impact of national culture on work; changing culture; whether culture can be managed; the dark side of culture
Unit 8 Organisational change: triggers for change; understanding change; change management; change management models; the people aspects of change
theories: Unit 1: scientific management (Taylor); bureaucracy (Weber); administrative management (Fayol); the human relations school and the Hawthorne studies (Mayo); systems and contingency approaches; Mintzberg's managerial roles; Theory X and Theory Y (McGregor)

Unit 2: the Big Five personality model; the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator; multiple intelligences (Gardner); emotional intelligence (Goleman); fixed and growth mindsets (Dweck); cognitive dissonance (Festinger); attribution theory (Heider; Kelley); perceptual biases such as the halo effect, stereotyping and selective perception; the self-fulfilling prophecy; neurodiversity and person-job fit

Unit 3: Maslow's hierarchy of needs; Alderfer's ERG theory; Herzberg's two-factor theory; McClelland's acquired needs; expectancy theory (Vroom); equity theory (Adams); goal-setting theory (Locke and Latham); self-determination theory (Deci and Ryan); the Job Characteristics Model (Hackman and Oldham); job enlargement, enrichment, rotation and crafting; performance management and feedback; employee engagement (Kahn); the job demands-resources model (Bakker and Demerouti); the psychological contract (Rousseau)

Unit 4: groups versus teams (Katzenbach and Smith); Tuckman's stages of group development; Belbin's team roles; group norms and cohesiveness; groupthink (Janis); social loafing (Ringelmann); conformity (Asch); Lencioni's five dysfunctions of a team; psychological safety (Edmondson); virtual and hybrid teams

Unit 5: French and Raven's bases of power; Lukes's three dimensions of power; resource dependence (Pfeffer and Salancik); organisational politics and political tactics (Pfeffer; Mintzberg's political games); unitarist, pluralist and radical perspectives on conflict (Fox); the Thomas-Kilmann conflict modes; functional and dysfunctional conflict (Pondy)

Unit 6: dimensions of structure (specialisation, centralisation, formalisation, span of control, chain of command); functional, divisional, matrix and network structures; mechanistic and organic organisations (Burns and Stalker); contingency theory (Woodward; Lawrence and Lorsch); Mintzberg's organisational configurations; Galbraith's Star Model; the formal and the informal organisation

Unit 7: Schein's three levels of culture; Handy's four culture types; Deal and Kennedy's culture model; the Competing Values Framework (Cameron and Quinn); the cultural web (Johnson and Scholes); Hofstede's cultural dimensions; Trompenaars's dimensions; culture as something an organisation has versus something it is (Smircich); toxic culture and the dark side of strong cultures

Unit 8: internal and external triggers for change (PESTLE); planned versus emergent change; incremental versus transformational change; Lewin's three-step model and force field analysis; Kotter's eight-step model; the ADKAR model; the McKinsey 7S framework; the change curve (Kübler-Ross); resistance to change and Kotter and Schlesinger's strategies; Bridges's transition model

name: Leadership Theory and Practice
focus: Leadership theories and their practice, power and influence, ethics and responsibility, decision making, leading change, developing leaders, followership.
theories: The Blake and Mouton managerial grid

name: Delivering Successful Projects
focus: Project life cycle, scope, time and cost, planning and scheduling, risk and stakeholder management, governance, agile and waterfall methods, benefits realisation, why projects fail.
theories: The project life cycle and stage gates
Work breakdown structure, critical path method and PERT
Project risk management and the risk register
The planning fallacy and reference class forecasting (Kahneman; Flyvbjerg)

name: Developing and Executing Strategy
focus: Competitive advantage, analysis of the industry and environment, resources and capabilities, strategic choices, growth, mergers and alliances, business models, and turning strategy into execution.

name: Financial Decision Making
focus: Financial statements and ratios, working capital and cash flow, investment appraisal, cost of capital, capital structure, budgeting, risk management, valuation.
theories: Net present value, internal rate of return and payback
The weighted average cost of capital and CAPM
Capital structure theory (Modigliani and Miller, trade-off, pecking order)
Working capital management and the cash conversion cycle
Ratio analysis and the DuPont model
Risk and return and portfolio theory (Markowitz)

name: Strategic Marketing
focus: Segmentation, targeting and positioning, brands, the marketing mix, pricing, customer experience and loyalty, consumer behaviour, digital marketing, market research.
theories: Customer-based brand equity (Keller) and Aaker's brand equity model
Relationship marketing and customer lifetime value

name: Global Purchasing and Supply
focus: Procurement strategy, global sourcing, supplier selection and relationships, make-or-buy and outsourcing, category management, negotiation, purchasing risk, ethical and sustainable sourcing.
theories: Supplier relationship management and the partnership spectrum
Global sourcing, offshoring, nearshoring and reshoring

name: Strategies for Managing Supply Chains
focus: Supply chain strategy and design, integration and collaboration, demand and inventory management, lean and agile approaches, risk and resilience, performance measurement.
theories: Fisher's supply chain matrix (functional vs innovative products)
The bullwhip effect (Lee, Padmanabhan and Whang)
Lean, agile and leagile supply chains (Christopher; Naylor)
Supply chain integration and the arcs of integration (Frohlich and Westbrook)
Supply chain risk management and resilience (Christopher and Peck)
Slack's five performance objectives and the theory of constraints (Goldratt)

name: Green and Sustainable Logistics
focus: The environmental and social impact of logistics: emissions from freight transport and warehousing, decarbonisation, modal shift, reverse logistics, the circular economy, regulation and reporting.
theories: Carbon footprinting and Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions
McKinnon's green logistics framework for decarbonising freight
Reverse logistics and closed-loop supply chains

name: Logistics Operations: Freight Transport and Warehouse Management
focus: Freight transport modes and networks, carriers and shipping, ports, warehousing, distribution centres, automation, inventory control, outsourcing to logistics providers, logistics costs and service.
theories: Modal choice and the trade-off between transport cost and service
Distribution network design: hub-and-spoke, cross-docking and consolidation
Warehouse layout, slotting and order picking methods
ABC inventory analysis, economic order quantity and safety stock
Logistics outsourcing: third-party and fourth-party logistics
Total logistics cost and the cost-service trade-off
Logistics performance measures such as on-time in-full
Warehouse automation and warehouse management systems

name: Humanitarian Logistics
focus: Logistics for disaster relief and development aid: preparedness and response, relief supply chains, coordination between agencies, donors and governments, last-mile distribution in crises.
theories: The disaster management cycle (mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery)
Van Wassenhove's humanitarian supply chain preparedness framework
Agility versus leanness in relief supply chains
Swift trust in hastily formed networks
